verdict.rationale: DBOS documents an OpenAPI-described HTTP API for Conductor covering workflow, queue, schedule, application, metrics, audit-log, member and API-key management. A CLI client (dbosctl) and a programmatic DBOSClient also let external code drive the product. The probe's 404s on docs.dbos.dev OpenAPI paths only show the spec isn't hosted at those URLs; they do not contradict the documented API. Missing for 10: a publicly locatable OpenAPI spec file, independent or hands-on corroboration of the HTTP API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Conductor's workflow, queue, and schedule management is available over an OpenAPI-described HTTP API and from the dbosctl command-line client, so you can script incident response and wire Conductor into your own tooling.

register applications with Conductor and tune their settings, search workflows, cancel or fork them, inspect queues and schedules, drive schedules, read metrics and audit logs, and manage members, roles, and API keys.
DBOSClient provides a programmatic way to interact with your DBOS application from external code or from another DBOS application.
